This was a document disclosed to the Defence, is a P exhibit, so I assume the Prosecution knows the source, and that's why they disclosed it. I want to refer to certain points in the document that might be known to the witness, and I would really appreciate it if Mr. Scott would let me finish my cross-examination today, and maybe he can make his objection when I tender the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, Counsel, and I'm not trying to be, you know, funny about it. If it came from the OTP that may be well and good, and I'll certainly check on that, and then I accept Counsel's representation on it. I don't -- I still don't see and as I sit here in the courtroom, I don't see the source or any information about where the document came from itself, not whether you got it from the OTP but where the document came from. I just thought you perhaps could assist the courtroom with that information. That's all I was suggesting -- asking, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot be sure. My colleagues are helping me in trying to establish that, but I believe the document is on the 65 ter list. However, it's indisputable that we got it from the OTP together with their translation. It has an ERN number, and I suppose it's not a problem to check where it is from. The document is in e-court. My colleague tells me it's on the 65 ter list, indeed. I am not trying to be ironic. It's on the Prosecution 65 ter list. I expected my learned friend to check first and then object if necessary. I was just trying to use my time efficiently and finish if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may assist, the Prosecution designates the source of this document as the municipal government on their 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now continue? I thank my colleague for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I refer to page 4 of this document. I'd like to ask you very briefly, and everybody can follow. This is a report from an intelligence officer on the developments in the area. It's the 27th April. It's an important date, I believe, and I'm just reminding you. On page 3 in Croatian, that is 00430013, this document proposes certain measures for the period to follow. On Croatian page 4, and that's ERN 00430015 in the translation, this document speaks of two axes of attack and says: "The second axis of attack is Obri and Kostajnica villages where it is necessary to completely rout HVO forces, disarm them, take all of them prisoners, and in that way, we would create on the other side an area where it would be possible to receive 18.000 Muslims who are now endangered on the left bank of the Neretva. Our fighting men would then be able to match much more successfully the forces of the joint Chetniks and Croats." I suppose this is a reference to the cleansing performed by BH army members. Let me ask you, did Konjic have the same number of refugees as Jablanica, and did this indeed happen? The expulsion of Croats and Muslims from Jablanica, did it lead to the creation of this free area for their accommodation, and was it indeed a way to perform ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm this because in the camp itself for six months there were at least 35 captive Croats from Obri and Kostajnica who told me their stories. If they hadn't told me I wouldn't have been aware this. But again I read in the diary of General Sefko Hodzic that was published in 22 instalments in Oslobodjenje newspaper writing about the operation Neretva and he mentioned a large number of Muslim refugees in Kostajnica and the problems that they had with accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll skip now certain documents that have been mentioned, and I believe I can go through them with other witnesses. If the usher would be so kind to get document 2D 1036. It should be the third document from the bottom. 2D 1036. If you found that document, I suppose you haven't seen it before, but this is a document of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the armed forces of BH, the 4th Corps command, the military security sector. The date is 9 February 1994. It pertains to the detainees held in the museum of Jablanica. The document is written by the chief of military security sector of the 4th Corps. I'm showing it to you so you can just confirm what you've said previously. The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina is holding civilians in the Jablanica museum as well, and that tallies with the testimony of Safet Idrizovic here in the courtroom. It says: "Urgently deliver a list of the captured Ustasha soldiers you are holding at the museum of Jablanica. Also submit the complete list of Croat civilians who are held at the museum in Jablanica. Along with name and surname, indicate the exact date and place of birth. This information is needed for the commission for exchange of war prisoners in Medjugorje in which exchange Jablanica is also involved." Can you confirm that there were not only members of the HVO but also civilians in Jablanica museum?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 80 or over 80 per cent civilians. The rest were HVO. I saw Mr. Selman who came and questioned certain soldiers, members of the HVO who were particularly interesting to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic said this about Dr. Cibo as well in document 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you confirm as this document does that these were indeed captive civilians that were not able to move around freely?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm they were prisoners who were not free to move around.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In conclusion, I want to show you another two documents, the last two. 2D 01441. It's from the 3rd Battalion, Mijat Tomic, Jablanica, Doljani. The date is 16 June 1993, and it speaks of the relationship between the UNPROFOR, UNHCR, and the ICRC on one hand and the HVO on the other. It's signed by Ivica Tomic, but that's not so important as are the facts indicated in that document. The second paragraph says: "The base of the UNHCR in Jablanica is in the premises of the Public Revenue Service, Public Auditing Service, where they have computers and other office equipment, and in return the BH army's using their communication equipment and mobile phones belonging to the UNHCR." Is it true that UNHCR placed their communications and other equipment to -- at the disposal of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, but I can confirm that in those offices of the SDK UNHCR was indeed stationed because the SDK was not working any more. And the author of this text, Mr. Tomic was killed on the 8th of July in the attack at Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This also mentions the representative of ICRC, Mark Deparot [phoen]. It says he's billeted in the house of Meho Manjusak, one of the most extremist men in Jablanica. Did you know this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO ZELENIKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the ICRC was in the house of Meho Manjusak. They even placed their flag on the house, but I don't know whether Manjusak was the greatest extremist or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 2D 01442 will be my last document. It speaks of the situation in Jablanica in the past three months, focusing on the last month. I know you were in captivity at the time, and this document is very relevant to that. It says that: "On the 31st October 1993, 22 of our soldiers escaped from the -- from detention in Jablanica." It's the centre of Sisak, Tomislavgrad. And the document -- sorry, it's the centre of SIS in Tomislavgrad and what they knew. It's the sixth line in Croatian, and the first paragraph in English. It says: "According to sources there is great discontent in the army and the civilian population. They have no fuel, and their food supplies are held by Zuka, who is selling them for Deutschmarks. Zuka also set up check-points facing Jablanica and Konjic. His soldiers are mainly from Sandzak and the recently released prisoners from Dretelj." I need literally two minutes to finish with this document. If we could move into private session. I remember that the witness gave evidence on this in private session. I don't want to compromise his safety. But I will be done in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Wait a moment, Counsel. Time's up. We have to finish. I have to read a short decision, so you will ask your question tomorrow. A decision, the oral decision is the following: On the 13th October the Prosecution asked that the cross-examination be put back to another date because it wanted to cross-examine on the basis of conversations with Cvikl for his expert report. The Chamber considers this request is premature because Prosecution has not replied to the expert report. According to Article -- Rule 94 bis (B), according to Defence Prlic is requested to put in another date at the end of November 2008. Therefore, the Chamber decides that the cross-examination of the Zelenika witness has to continue this week as agreed. That is to say tomorrow and rejects the request of Prosecution to postpone to another date. The Chamber also decides not to decide on the request of the Prosecution for a cross-examination of the witness on the conversations he may have had with Witness Cvikl at a later date. So cross-examination of the Prosecutor will start tomorrow, and if ever the Prosecution still has the intention to ask questions from the witness on the conversations he may have had with Mr. Cvikl, we will see that at a later date. So tomorrow we will resume the question of Mrs. Nozica and her document, but we have already gone further than the time and there's a Chamber coming at a quarter past 2.00. So we will finish with Counsel Nozica tomorrow, and then Ms. Alaburic will continue, and then Mr. Scott will start his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: examined by the panel mentioned in this document.
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
